notice: Original app practice. Section lengths and 30/20/15 minute timers are app choices, not official exam allocations or a complete syllabus assessment. Physical observations and written criteria are learner-led; no official marks or qualification are granted.

mcqs.prompt: A list has Chablis beside a Sauvignon Blanc from the Loire. Which grape distinguishes the Chablis entry?
mcqs.explanation: Chablis uses Chardonnay; a Loire Sauvignon entry does not change that identity.

mcqs.prompt: A guest asks which grape connects Barolo with its Piedmont identity. Which answer is supported?
mcqs.explanation: The Barolo grape is Nebbiolo, not another Italian red variety.

mcqs.prompt: Which country contains the Mosel wine-growing region?
mcqs.explanation: Mosel is a German wine-growing region.

mcqs.prompt: What distinguishes the grape condition used for German Eiswein?

options.text: Nobly rotten berries selected after fermentation
Naturally frozen at picking and pressing

mcqs.explanation: The defining condition is naturally frozen grapes at harvest and pressing, not artificial freezing or drying.

mcqs.prompt: What does high elevation explain in the cited Gualtallary vineyard comparison?

options.text: Moderated temperature compared with warmer lower sites
A legal guarantee of superior wine quality
The absence of vineyard and cellar decisions

mcqs.explanation: The cited Adrianna comparison treats altitude as a temperature influence, not a quality ranking.

mcqs.prompt: Which account respects the Barossa valley-floor and hill-site comparison?

options.text: Every site has identical temperatures and style
Warmer valley floors and cooler surrounding hill sites
All Shiraz must be sweet because the valley is warm
Altitude determines the legal grape recipe

mcqs.explanation: The warm floor supports ripe Shiraz, but cooler sites and production choices prevent a single universal profile.

mcqs.prompt: What limits a single aroma prediction for Wairau Sauvignon Blanc?

options.text: The regional name requires identical picking dates
Every vineyard must use the same oak regime
Contrasting inland and coastal growing sites
Sauvignon Blanc is excluded from the valley

mcqs.explanation: Stony inland and sea-breeze-moderated coastal sites vary; the regional association does not fix one aroma.

mcqs.prompt: Compared with the Wairau reference, how is Awatere generally framed?

options.text: Always warmer with no elevated vineyards

mcqs.explanation: The reference generally describes cooler, drier, windier conditions, while individual sites and harvest choices still matter.

mcqs.prompt: Which principal products come from wine yeast metabolising grape sugar?
mcqs.explanation: Alcoholic fermentation principally forms ethanol and carbon dioxide; MLF is different.

mcqs.prompt: Which conversion identifies malolactic fermentation rather than alcoholic fermentation?

options.text: Lactic acid to harvested grape sugar

mcqs.explanation: Lactic acid bacteria convert malic acid into lactic acid, commonly reducing acidity.

mcqs.prompt: Why is a buttery aroma insufficient to predict all wines that undergo MLF?

options.text: MLF requires identical buttery intensity in every wine
Butter aroma measures the legal vineyard boundary
Diacetyl impact varies with strain, timing and wine conditions
MLF always removes every aroma compound

mcqs.explanation: Diacetyl can contribute butter aroma, but its sensory impact varies and is not inevitable.

mcqs.prompt: Which information best refines a guess about oak influence?

options.text: Only the nationality of the cooper
Only the colour of the bottle closure
Only the grape region printed on the label
Wood species, toast, vessel size and barrel age

mcqs.explanation: Species, toast, size, barrel age and cooperage all matter; origin alone cannot determine flavour.

mcqs.prompt: Which base-and-vermouth pair identifies the IBA Dry Martini reference?
mcqs.explanation: The named IBA reference uses gin and dry vermouth, stirred; venue and guest variants require checking.

mcqs.prompt: A guest wants the IBA Campari-vermouth reference extended with soda, without gin. Which name fits?
mcqs.explanation: Americano combines Campari, sweet red vermouth and soda without added gin.

mcqs.prompt: What is the useful starch-related purpose of mashing malt for beer?

options.text: Yeast directly distils the dry grain
Hops convert sugar into barrel tannin
Enzymes convert starch into fermentable sugars

mcqs.explanation: Malt enzymes make fermentable sugars available through starch conversion during mashing.

mcqs.prompt: Which fruit is central to the cider-production reference here?
mcqs.explanation: Cider reference production begins with apples; this is not a universal duty-law definition.

mcqs.prompt: In the supplied hypothetical example, 750 mL is divided into complete 100 mL pours. How many full pours fit?
mcqs.explanation: Floor(750/100)=7, leaving 50 mL; the pour size is supplied, not a legal standard.

mcqs.prompt: A hypothetical event requires 40 guests x 2 pours x 125 mL. Pool wine from 750 mL bottles, no loss/reserve. What is the minimum whole-bottle count?
mcqs.explanation: The required 10,000 mL is 13 and 1/3 bottles, rounded up to 14 whole bottles.

mcqs.prompt: A hypothetical bottle sells net of tax for EUR 30 and has EUR 12 cost of goods. What gross margin results?
mcqs.explanation: Gross profit 18 divided by sales 30 gives 60%; 150% instead uses cost as markup denominator.

mcqs.prompt: A hypothetical bottle costs EUR 12; no discounts/tax/fees apply. Which net price produces 60% gross margin?
mcqs.explanation: Price=12/(1-0.60)=30; adding 60% to cost would not achieve 60% margin.

written.prompt: Name the grape of Chablis and distinguish it from a Sauvignon Blanc Loire wine.

criteria.text: Identify Chardonnay; do not call Chablis Sauvignon Blanc.

written.prompt: Name the grape used for Barolo, rather than a nearby Italian variety.

criteria.text: Identify Nebbiolo for Barolo.

written.prompt: Locate Mosel by country without substituting a different German district.

criteria.text: Name Germany for the Mosel region.

written.prompt: Describe the required grape condition for German Eiswein, without treating indoor freezing as equivalent.

criteria.text: State grapes must be naturally frozen when picked and pressed.

written.prompt: Explain why a high-elevation Gualtallary site can differ from warmer lower sites and state one inference limit.

criteria.text: Link elevation to moderated temperature, while withholding a guaranteed quality ranking.

written.prompt: Explain why Barossa Shiraz cannot be assigned one style solely from the regional name.

criteria.text: Distinguish warmer valley-floor and cooler hill settings, with vineyard and winery choices affecting balance.

written.prompt: Name two contrasting Wairau site influences and explain why the label alone cannot fix aroma.

criteria.text: Contrast inland early-ripening stony sites with coastal sea-breeze influence; avoid one compulsory aroma profile.

written.prompt: Compare the Awatere and Wairau climate references, retaining a site-specific limit.

criteria.text: Describe Awatere as generally cooler, drier and windier; do not turn the comparison into one guaranteed flavour.

written.prompt: Name the principal fermentation products from grape sugars.

criteria.text: Identify ethanol and carbon dioxide.

written.prompt: Describe MLF and distinguish it from yeast fermentation of sugars.

criteria.text: Identify bacterial malic-to-lactic conversion, distinct from sugar-to-alcohol fermentation.

written.prompt: State why MLF does not guarantee a buttery finished wine.

criteria.text: Mention variable diacetyl production/sensory impact and reject inevitable butter aroma.

written.prompt: Give three variables affecting oak influence, and explain why origin alone is insufficient.

criteria.text: Name at least three of species, toast, vessel size, barrel age or cooperage; retain the inference limit.

written.prompt: State the IBA Dry Martini ingredient pair and its reference mixing method.

criteria.text: Name gin and dry vermouth, stirred rather than a universal venue recipe.

written.prompt: Distinguish the IBA Americano reference from Negroni for a guest avoiding gin.

criteria.text: Americano adds soda and omits gin; Negroni includes gin.

written.prompt: Explain the starch-to-sugar role of malt enzymes during mashing.

criteria.text: Describe enzymatic conversion of starch into fermentable sugars, rather than distillation.

written.prompt: Name cider fruit and distinguish its fermentation from distilled spirit production.

criteria.text: Identify apples and fermentation, without turning the example into a worldwide legal definition.

written.prompt: For the hypothetical 750 mL bottle and 100 mL pour, calculate full pours and leftover volume.

criteria.text: Give 7 complete pours and 50 mL leftover; no partial pour counts.

written.prompt: Calculate minimum 750 mL bottles for 40 guests receiving two 125 mL pours, ignoring losses/reserve and pooling usable wine.

criteria.text: Compute 10,000 mL and round 13 and 1/3 up to 14 whole bottles.

written.prompt: Calculate gross margin for hypothetical EUR 30 net sales and EUR 12 cost, stating the denominator.

criteria.text: Gross profit 18 divided by net sales 30 equals 60%; do not use cost as denominator.

written.prompt: Find tax-exclusive price for EUR 12 cost and 60% target gross margin in the stated hypothetical example.

criteria.text: Use 12/(1-0.60)=EUR 30; distinguish margin from adding 60% markup.

written.prompt: A fictional guest requests a Campari-and-vermouth aperitif with soda, says no gin, and has not specified the preferred balance or ingredient restrictions. Recommend a reference drink, explain its fit, discuss an alternative only if the preference changes, and identify checks before service.

criteria.text: Offer Americano provisionally and confirm the actual venue recipe.
Explain soda without gin distinguishes Americano from the Negroni reference.
Discuss Negroni only if the no-gin preference changes.
Check stocked recipe and guest ingredient suitability; a reference cannot establish them.

written.prompt: A fictional guest wants rum and lime without orange liqueur. The bar has the named IBA Daiquiri and Margarita reference ingredients. Recommend provisionally, explain the recipe distinction, discuss a conditional alternative and identify information needed about the actual guest and drink.

criteria.text: Offer Daiquiri and clarify the desired balance.
Distinguish rum-lime-sugar from tequila-triple-sec-lime.
Margarita becomes relevant only if tequila and triple sec are acceptable.
Check the actual recipe and guest taste rather than promising the reference measures suit everyone.

written.prompt: A fictional guest prefers crisp dry still white with oysters dressed in lemon and vinegar. Consider a Muscadet trial, explain the dressing interaction, discuss a conditional alternative and state why the exact bottle and plate still need checking.

criteria.text: Suggest Muscadet as a tentative tasting trial, respecting the still-white preference.
Consider the acidity of lemon/vinegar when judging wine balance.
Offer Champagne only if the guest wants that alternative.
Do not guarantee every condiment-and-bottle combination from a general reference.

written.prompt: A fictional guest likes fortified wine and orders high-cocoa chocolate tart with salted caramel. Consider a Tawny Port trial, explain sweetness, discuss the salt/topping tradeoff and state the evidence still missing.

criteria.text: Offer Tawny Port as a provisional trial.
Sweet food can make a dry wine seem less fruity, drier and more bitter.
Account for salt and caramel as well as cocoa in the actual dish.
The cited example does not test this exact tart or stocked bottle.

written.prompt: Compare the two actual wines you tasted. Separate direct observations from grape/origin hypotheses, show which structure or aroma evidence supports each, note any possible fault in its style context, and record what remains uncertain. No app answer establishes the bottle identity.

criteria.text: Use recorded observations from both wines; do not infer one uniform regional aroma from a name.
Support a production hypothesis with observations while recognising that MLF and alcoholic fermentation are different mechanisms.
Discuss possible oxidation in its intended-style context rather than declaring every developed aroma a fault.
State uncertainty and a useful next check; oak provenance alone cannot fix final flavour or bottle identity.

wineEvidencePrompts.prompt: Describe this actual wine using your own sensory observations, separating fruit and other aromas.
Explain the observed acidity, tannin, alcohol, body and finish; support your interpretation with sensations.
Propose grape and origin hypotheses and explain which observations support them; record a plausible alternative.
Explain your quality judgement and any suspected fault with observations and intended-style context.
State which identity, age or production inference remains uncertain and what could help check it.
